LESSON: LEADERSHIP IN ISRAEL: SAUL

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible 2.2 Abrahamic Covenant (6 lessons) By the end of the sub- strand, the 
Topic 2.3: Leadership in Israel: Saul

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Leadership in Israel: Saul. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how they exercise leadership qualities at school and in church. Why did King Saul fail in his leadership?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. discuss reasons for kingship in Israel
2. describe the healing of blind Bartimaeus
3. discuss lessons learnt from the healing of blind Bartimaeus
4. apply lessons learnt when faced with health challenges

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LEADERSHIP IN ISRAEL: SAUL
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Leadership in Israel: Saul helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: LEADERSHIP IN ISRAEL: SAUL
Study Leadership in Israel: Saul like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Discuss reasons for kingship in Israel

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss reasons for kingship in Israel. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss reasons for kingship in Israel.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Leadership in Israel: Saul” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss reasons for kingship in Israel. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the healing of blind Bartimaeus

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the healing of blind Bartimaeus. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the healing of blind Bartimaeus.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Leadership in Israel: Saul in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the healing of blind Bartimaeus. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Discuss lessons learnt from the healing of blind Bartimaeus

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss lessons learnt from the healing of blind Bartimaeus. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss lessons learnt from the healing of blind Bartimaeus.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss lessons learnt from the healing of blind Bartimaeus. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply lessons learnt when faced with health challenges

What this means
In this part you learn to apply lessons learnt when faced with health challenges. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply lessons learnt when faced with health challenges.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Leadership in Israel: Saul” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply lessons learnt when faced with health challenges. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Leadership in Israel: Saul is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Leadership in Israel: Saul” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: discuss reasons for kingship in Israel)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Leadership in Israel: Saul in your own words. (skill: describe the healing of blind Bartimaeus)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: discuss lessons learnt from the healing of blind Bartimaeus)

Example 4: Show how “Leadership in Israel: Saul” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply lessons learnt when faced with health challenges)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Leadership in Israel: Saul to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: discuss reasons for kingship in Israel.
3. Practise this skill: describe the healing of blind Bartimaeus.
4. Practise this skill: discuss lessons learnt from the healing of blind Bartimaeus.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Leadership in Israel: Saul from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Leadership in Israel: Saul: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Leadership in Israel: Saul?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how they exercise leadership qualities at school and in church. Why did King Saul fail in his leadership?
2. How does the healing of blind Bartimaeus build your faith in God?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Leadership in Israel: Saul means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: discuss reasons for kingship in Israel.
5. Be able to: describe the healing of blind Bartimaeus.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
